Evidence: The reported line 42 uses userCookie.setDomain(new java.net.URL(request.getRequestURL().toString()).getHost()) and the surrounding code window (lines 34-47) shows no guard, filter, or validation before the call. Gap: none.
findings.snippet: userCookie.setDomain(new java.net.URL(request.getRequestURL().toString()).getHost());
findings.issue: Host Header Injection leads to Cookie Domain Manipulation

findings.triage_reason: Verdict: The finding is valid because user-controlled cookie input is directly concatenated into the SQL query string on line 73 and executed via PreparedStatement with only the USERNAME placeholder parameterized, leaving the PASSWORD value unsanitized. Evidence: The cookie value retrieved at line 60 (java.net.URLDecoder.decode(theCookie.getValue(), "UTF-8")) is stored in 'param', propagated through a HashMap to 'bar' (line 71), and concatenated into the SQL string on line 73. The SQL string is passed to connection.prepareStatement() at line 79, and only statement.setString(1, "foo") sets the USERNAME placeholder (line 84); the PASSWORD portion remains embedded user input. statement.execute() at line 85 executes the unsanitized query. No validation, escaping, or parameterization is applied to the PASSWORD fragment. Gap: none.
findings.issue: SQL Injection in doPost method via concatenation of cookie value into SQL query

findings.triage_reason: Verdict: The cookie domain is directly derived from the request URL parsed via request.getRequestURL(), and the cookie path is directly set from request.getRequestURI(), both without any validation, allowlisting, or sanitization, enabling domain/path injection. Evidence: The code at lines 41-42 of BenchmarkTest00100.java shows userCookie.setPath(request.getRequestURI()) (line 41) and userCookie.setDomain(new java.net.URL(request.getRequestURL().toString()).getHost()) (line 42) with no guards or sanitizers in the same method window (lines 33-47). Gap: none.
findings.snippet:
userCookie.setPath(request.getRequestURI());
userCookie.setDomain(new java.net.URL(request.getRequestURL().toString()).getHost());
findings.issue: Cookie domain set from user-controllable request URL may allow domain injection
